messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — I'm opening a docs PR to refresh the onboarding flow for the new Hello Miniflow quickstart. Main changes: switch auth snippets from session-cookie examples to token-based env var flow, rename env var to REDWOOD_API_KEY, and swap the single-step docker run example for a devcontainer + local-compose approach. PR: #4281. Looking for a reviewer and a sanity check on the auth wording.
aj: Thanks — strong 👍 on moving to token env var. Can you paste the updated snippet here so I can sanity check before full review? Also call out any breaking changes for existing users.
devon: @maria small note: we should keep a short migration blurb — "If you used SESSION_TOKEN before, set REDWOOD_API_KEY=..." — but avoid implying server-side cookie support is removed. Some customers still rely on it.
maria: sure. snippet below (paste):

```
# .env
REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_live_XXXX

# example usage (Python)
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'])
resp = client.chat.create(model="redwood-alpha", input="Hello world")
print(resp.text)
```

maria: Breaking impact: none for hosted quickstart users (we're just showing a recommended token-based example). For Dedicated customers using session cookies, added a short note under "Auth options" linking to dedicated docs.
samir: I'll review wording for the "store api keys securely" note. Suggest small change: add one sentence about using KMS/HSM for Private deployments and link to /enterprise/auth. Also add a short example of setting env var in devcontainer.json for the quickstart.
aj: Couple of tiny phrasing suggestions: 1) Change "set REDWOOD_API_KEY" -> "set REDWOOD_API_KEY in your environment or secret store"; 2) Add a command for local-compose: `docker compose up --build hello-miniflow` so people can follow the first-run flow.
maria: updated PR patch with both changes and the devcontainer snippet. pinged @devon for migration blurb approval. Also added a link-check action to CI for any broken anchors in the todo list.
devon: LGTM on migration blurb. One more: please ensure the quickstart still uses the lightweight model by default (we shouldn't recommend a large model in the hello flow). Maybe `redwood-small` or `redwood-mini` depending on naming.
maria: Good catch — switched to `redwood-mini` in examples. Updated PR description to mention model name fix and added a short eval check to README: "expected first-run latency < 250ms" (informational).
docs-bot: CI status — PR #4281: lint: passed, link-check: passed, preview-site: generated at https://deploy-preview-4281--docs.redwood.ai
samir: Reviewing now. I left two tiny copy nits inline. Overall, this looks like a clean, low-risk onboarding refresh — thanks! :tada:
aj: If all green, can one of you merge after your reviews? I can do a quick smoke deploy to staging.
maria: Will wait for final thumbs. Thanks all.
docs-bot: Auto-merge scheduled: when approvals >= 2 and CI green. (status: pending)
samir: Approved. :shipit:
devon: Approved.
maria: Merged — thanks everyone. I'll open a follow-up to backfill a short migration note into the migration guide and add a tiny e2e test for the quickstart that runs `hello-miniflow` in CI container (smoke).
